acceptanceCriteria: A pull request whose own unbounded-readers-check passes cannot leave main failing that check after merge, or the failure is detected and attributed before the merge completes; retained evidence shows the case of an unbounded test package added to main after the pull request's last CI run.
body: Confirmed 2026-10-04 at origin/main 6bf78ff76889519d43b34cc2a5dfbf42b72e9ba9 (merge of pull request 530; macOS and a clean detached worktree, go1.27.1). Reproduce: `make unbounded-readers-check` on that revision. Actual: `unbounded-readers: 56 test units are selected on every change, above the ceiling 45 in .corvint/unbounded-readers.json`, exit 1; the check is a doc-gates step, so every pull request based on that main fails. Expected: main passes its own required gate. Cause: the ceiling was measured on the pull request branch; eleven unbounded test packages (cmd/corvint-cem-candidate, cmd/corvint-test-runner, internal/cem/gitauth, internal/cemcandidate, internal/testrunner and its dynamic, mobile, native, platform, registry, sql subpackages) reached main after the branch's last CI run, and the pull request merged without a run against the newer base. The immediate break is repaired by declaring read scopes (build log 2026-10-04-unbounded-reader-merge-skew), but the same skew recurs whenever a package that is unbounded merges while another pull request's passing check is stale; with the ceiling equal to the count there is no slack. Options to weigh: require branches to be up to date before merge, a merge queue, or have the main-push run report the skew with the offending packages. Related: V1-0719, V1-0728.
title: affected: unbounded-readers ratchet breaks main when an unbounded package merges after a pull request's last CI run
